# Project rules: electrical shop inventory SaaS

The team is Prashant plus Claude Code, which builds, reviews and researches.
Edit only this file and the files in `roles/`, then run `pnpm rules:sync`.
Never edit CLAUDE.md by hand: it is generated.

## Product

- Multi-tenant inventory and billing SaaS for Indian shops.
- First customer type: electrical and electronics shops (the "electrical preset").
- One generic inventory core; shop-type behaviour comes from module switches, never from code that checks the shop type.
- Owner and final decision-maker: Prashant. Only Prashant merges, deploys and holds secrets.

## Stack

- Frontend: Angular 21, standalone components, Signals, new control flow. UI: Angular Material (components, themed with our own Material 3 theme) plus Bootstrap for layout only (grid and utility classes; no Bootstrap components, no Bootstrap JavaScript). Do not add PrimeNG or other component libraries.
- Backend: NestJS (TypeScript).
- Database: PostgreSQL with row-level security on every tenant table.
- Jobs and cache: Redis with BullMQ.
- Repository: pnpm monorepo with `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `packages/shared`.
- Hosting: none paid until the pilot. The app runs production-like on the local PC from the CI-built Docker image; AWS Mumbai later (see DECISIONS.md).
- PWA: the web app is installable (Angular service worker, web manifest, icons), caches only the app shell and static assets, shows an update prompt and an offline page. Never cache API responses that carry shop data. Offline billing is not in the MVP.
- Open choices (ORM, auth provider, payment gateway, host) are listed in DECISIONS.md. Do not pick one silently.

## Data rules

- Money is integer paise. Quantities are NUMERIC(14,3). Never use floating point for either.
- Never update a stock quantity directly. Insert a `stock_movements` row and update the cached `on_hand` in the same transaction.
- The tenant is the shop. Every shop-owned table has `shop_id` and `UNIQUE (shop_id, id)`; references between them are composite `(shop_id, x_id)` foreign keys. Every query is scoped to the current shop. RLS (`ENABLE` and `FORCE`) on every shop-owned table, using `current_setting('app.shop_id', true)`. The API connects as a role without superuser or `BYPASSRLS`.
- The schema design is docs/schema.dbml; read docs/SCHEMA_NOTES.md before adding a table.
- Issued bills are immutable. Cancel with a reason or issue a credit note.
- Freeze price, MRP and tax rate on each document line at the time of sale.
- Store timestamps in UTC, show them in IST. Show dates as DD/MM/YYYY. Format amounts with ₹ and lakh/crore grouping through the shared helper only.
- All UI text goes through translation files (en, hi). No hard-coded labels.
- Module switches: `batch_tracking`, `serial_tracking`, `decimal_qty`, `price_lists`, `quotations`, `credit_ledger`, `expiry_tracking`, `pharmacy_compliance`.

## Electrical shop rules

- Wire is stored in metres (base unit). A coil is a batch row with its remaining metres.
- A sale draws from the open coil first, then the next. A coil never goes below zero.
- Serial-tracked items have one `serials` row per unit, with status `in_stock`, `sold`, `returned` or `in_service`. A serial can be sold only from `in_stock`.
- Warranty end = invoice date (IST) + the item's warranty months, computed once per sale and stored on that sale's `serial_sales` row. Brand and shop warranty are stored separately.
- Prices come from the customer's price list, falling back to the item's list price.
- Each role has a maximum discount. A discount above it needs a manager PIN. Warn when price is below cost.
- Quotations move no stock and use their own number series.
- A product has variants (brand, rating, finish). Stock, price and serials belong to the variant.
- Two stores per shop by default: godown and counter. Every movement belongs to a store.

## Indian compliance

- GST type per shop: regular -> tax invoice; composition -> bill of supply with the required declaration line; unregistered -> cash memo.
- HSN code on every item. The required length depends on the shop's turnover band.
- Same state: CGST + SGST. Other state: IGST. Store the customer's state on B2B bills.
- One invoice number series per financial year (April to March). Quotations have a separate series.
- Warn (or block, per shop setting) when a selling price is above MRP.
- DPDP: collect minimal personal data; per-shop export and delete; audit log of sensitive actions.
- Tax and legal facts must come from official sources (GST portal, CBIC, government text). Mark anything unverified as unverified. A CA confirms invoice formats before real shops use them.

## Security

- No secrets in code, commits, logs or prompts. Use environment variables, validated at start-up.
- Never connect to production, run destructive database commands, or change hosting settings. Prashant does those.
- Validate all input at the API boundary. Parameterized queries only. Rate-limit auth and public endpoints.
- The frontend never decides access; the API checks permissions on every route.

## Design

- Angular Material components only, themed through our design tokens (Material 3 theme). Bootstrap only for grid, spacing and other utility classes; when Bootstrap and Material overlap, Material wins.
- The billing screen is keyboard-first and works with a USB barcode scanner.
- Every screen works on a 1366x768 laptop and a 360 px wide mid-range Android phone.
- Every list screen has loading, empty and error states, pagination and search.
- Follow docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md for every new screen.

## How we work

1. One branch per feature: `feature/<name>`. Every change goes through a pull request. Only Prashant merges.
2. Plan before code for anything bigger than a small fix, and wait for approval.
3. Add tests with every change to stock, tax, serials, billing or tenancy.
4. Decisions go in DECISIONS.md. Do not reopen a recorded decision without new evidence.
5. When a rule is unclear, ask. When you finish, list what you did not verify.

## Reviews

Claude never reviews code in the same context that wrote it. A review runs as a separate reviewer agent that sees only the diff, these rules, DECISIONS.md and BACKLOG.md.

- Level 0 (text, styling, docs, pipeline config): no review. CI must pass. Prashant glances and merges.
- Level 1 (normal features): one fresh-context review before the PR is marked ready.
- Level 2 (stock, coils, serials, billing, tax, tenancy, auth, security): one fresh-context code review plus one security review, and all tests must pass.
- Phase-gate audit (end of Phase 2, 3 and 5): a whole-repository review against these rules and the phase gate.
- At most two rounds per pull request: one review, one fix. A second round only for a high-severity finding still open. Then Prashant decides.
- Only high and medium findings block a merge. Low findings go to BACKLOG.md and are fixed in batches.
- Each finding names a file, a line, a severity and a concrete failing case or risk. At most 10 findings, most severe first. Formatting and style are left to the formatter and linter.
- Claude checks each finding before acting: real ones are fixed, wrong ones go in DECISIONS.md as rejected with the evidence. Do not repeat a finding already rejected there or listed in BACKLOG.md.
- The PR description lists the review's findings and what happened to each, so Prashant can see them before merging.
- Tie-break order: this rules file, then the tests, then the simpler option, then Prashant's call.

## Research

- Tax, legal and compliance facts come from official sources (GST portal, CBIC, government text), cited with a link and the date checked. Anything else is marked unverified.
- A CA still confirms invoice formats, and a native speaker or Prashant checks Hindi, before real shops use them.

## Commands

Use Node 22 (`.nvmrc`). Run from the repository root.

- `pnpm install`: install everything.
- `pnpm dev`: start Postgres (host port 5433) and Redis in Docker, then the API and web dev servers.
- `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`: run across all packages.
- Database setup, roles and the checklist for adding a shop-owned table: docs/DATABASE.md.
- `pnpm db:bootstrap`, then `pnpm db:migrate`, then `pnpm db:setup-app-role`: prepare a fresh local database (local and CI only).
- `pnpm test:e2e`: API end-to-end and shop-isolation tests; needs the database prepared as above.
- `pnpm --filter api db:generate`: write a migration after changing `apps/api/src/db/schema.ts`. Grants and RLS go in a custom SQL migration. Never edit a migration after merge.
- Database access in the API: shop-owned tables only through `withShop(db, shopId, tx => ...)` in `src/db/with-shop.ts`. Lint blocks setting the shop anywhere else.
- API docs (not in production): http://localhost:3000/docs. Health check: http://localhost:3000/health.
- Local settings: copy `.env.example` to `.env` at the repository root.
- `pnpm rules:sync`: regenerate CLAUDE.md after editing RULES.md or roles/.
